lobby.definition: A large entrance or reception room or area.

teller-window.definition: A bank service counter where a teller assists customers with permitted account transactions and questions.
teller-window.exampleUsage: The customer asked a question at the teller window.

vault.definition: A strongly secured room for storing money and valuable items.

safe-deposit-box.definition: A secure box rented from a bank or similar institution for storing important items or documents.
safe-deposit-box.exampleUsage: The bank keeps safe-deposit boxes in a secure area.

atm.definition: A machine that lets customers withdraw cash and carry out other banking transactions.

drive-through.definition: A service area where customers can receive assistance without leaving their vehicle.
drive-through.exampleUsage: The bank's drive-through lane is beside the branch.

office.definition: Place of business where professional or clerical duties are performed.

waiting-area.definition: A room in a place such as an airport or hotel where people sit until they are ready to leave or be served.

security-desk.definition: A staffed point where security personnel monitor entry, visitors, or safety procedures.
security-desk.exampleUsage: Visitors checked in at the security desk.

currency-exchange.definition: A business or institution that lets people trade one national currency for another.

checking-account.definition: A bank account designed for frequent payments, deposits, and withdrawals.
checking-account.exampleUsage: She used her checking account for everyday payments.

savings-account.definition: A bank account mainly intended for keeping money and potentially earning interest under the account terms.
savings-account.exampleUsage: She asked the bank about the interest and withdrawal conditions on her savings account.

joint-account.definition: A bank account legally held by two or more people.
joint-account.exampleUsage: The form explains the responsibilities of people on a joint account.

business-account.definition: A bank account intended for the financial transactions of a business or organization.
business-account.exampleUsage: The company keeps its operating funds in a business account.

certificate-of-deposit.definition: A bank deposit product held for a specified term under agreed interest and withdrawal conditions.
certificate-of-deposit.exampleUsage: The certificate of deposit has a stated maturity date.

money-market.definition: A financial market where institutions lend and borrow money for brief periods.

retirement-account.definition: A structured way to save and manage money for use once you leave the workforce.

student-account.definition: A bank account designed for eligible students, often with features or fees tailored to them.
student-account.exampleUsage: The brochure describes the conditions for a student account.

trust-account.definition: An account holding money managed for a beneficiary under a trust arrangement.

escrow.definition: Money or property held by a third party until agreed conditions are met.

deposit.definition: To put money into a bank account.

withdraw.definition: To take money out of a bank account.

transfer.definition: To move money from one account to another.

wire.definition: To send money electronically using a money-transfer service.

cash-check.definition: To exchange a valid check for cash through an authorized financial institution or service.
cash-check.exampleUsage: He asked the bank whether he could cash the check and what identification was required.

open-account.definition: To start a new bank account.

close-account.definition: To formally end a bank account so it is no longer active.
close-account.exampleUsage: The account holder asked the bank about the process to close the account.

apply-for-loan.definition: To submit a formal request to a lender to borrow money under stated terms.
apply-for-loan.exampleUsage: They asked which documents were required to apply for a loan.

pay-bill.definition: To send money to a company or person to settle an amount that is due.
pay-bill.exampleUsage: The account holder chose to pay the bill before its due date.

check-balance.definition: To view the amount of money currently recorded in an account.
check-balance.exampleUsage: The account holder checked the balance on the statement.

teller.definition: An employee of a bank who receives and pays out money.

bank-manager.definition: A person responsible for supervising the staff and operations of a bank branch.
bank-manager.exampleUsage: The bank manager reviewed branch operations.

loan-officer.definition: A financial-services employee who evaluates loan applications and explains lending requirements.
loan-officer.exampleUsage: The loan officer explained the loan documents to the adult applicant.

financial-advisor.definition: A professional who gives clients guidance about financial planning, investments, or related money decisions within their qualifications.
financial-advisor.exampleUsage: The financial advisor discussed long-term planning concepts with the family.

security-guard.definition: A person who protects a building and its people.

accountant.definition: A person who maintains and audits business accounts.

auditor.definition: A qualified accountant who inspects the accounting records and practices of a business or other organization.

branch-manager.definition: The manager responsible for a particular local branch of a bank or other organization.
branch-manager.exampleUsage: The branch manager supervised the staff meeting.

customer-service.definition: The people and work that guide buyers, handle orders, answer questions, and resolve complaints.

compliance-officer.definition: An employee who monitors whether an organization follows applicable laws, regulatory requirements, and its own policies.
compliance-officer.exampleUsage: The compliance officer reviewed the branch procedures.
